title: Stand Out, Don't Blend In: A Study of Ephesians 5:1-20
metaDescription: What does it look like to follow Christ in a broken world? A study of Ephesians 5:1-20 on living in love, walking in the light, and being filled with the Spirit.
bodyHtml:
Picture a chameleon. It is remarkable at one thing: blending in. It changes its colors to match whatever surrounds it so completely that you can barely tell it is there. But here is the catch — a chameleon never changes its surroundings. It only disappears into them. This past Sunday we asked a hard question: are we following Jesus in a way that changes the world around us, or are we simply changing colors to blend in?

Continuing our series Grace for You, we worked through Ephesians 5:1-20. Paul's message is simple but costly: you were not created to blend in — you were created to stand out. Not in a look-at-me, build-my-brand way, but in a way that brings glory to God, good to others, and even good to yourself. Here are three truths from the passage that help us do exactly that.

1. Let love lead to purity

Paul begins not with a rule but with an identity.

"Follow God's example, therefore, as dearly loved children and walk in the way of love, just as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us as a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God. But among you there must not be even a hint of sexual immorality, or of any kind of impurity, or of greed... nor should there be obscenity, foolish talk or coarse joking, which are out of place, but rather thanksgiving." (Ephesians 5:1-4)

Notice the order. Before Paul names any sin to avoid, he names who you are: a dearly loved child of God. Who you are is meant to shape how you live. You are not defined by your feelings, your failures, or even your best moments — you are defined by how your Father sees you in Christ.

From that love, Paul names three things that choke out love for God and others:

  • Sexual immorality — at its root, loving pleasure more than God and more than people, using others as objects instead of honoring them as image-bearers.
  • Greed — being possessed by your possessions, believing "enough" will finally satisfy, and neglecting people to chase more.
  • Obscenity and coarse joking — making light of what damages and dishonors people and God.

Then comes the line that lands hardest: "not even a hint." Imagine a delicious cake that someone admits contains "just a hint" of poison. You would not keep eating it. Yet we often nurse small sins — a glance, a flirtation at the office, a quiet compromise — telling ourselves it is harmless. Small sins have large consequences. God does not want to be followed partially, or even mostly; He wants your whole heart.

How do we actually resist? Not by white-knuckling our way to being better people, but by being so satisfied in God's love that sin loses its pull. When you have feasted on His grace, the counterfeit stops looking appealing. Love leads to purity.

2. Live in the light

"For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light... Have nothing to do with the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather expose them... everything exposed by the light becomes visible, and everything that is illuminated becomes a light." (Ephesians 5:8-14)

Living in the light means two things. First, do not be influenced by those in the dark. This is not a call to abandon relationships with people who do not follow Jesus — we are to be in the world, not of it. It is a call to stop partnering with sin. Love people; influence them for Christ rather than being pulled into compromise.

Second, let the light reveal the truth. Sin is like mold: it thrives in the dark and grows while hidden. Light exposes it — and remarkably, light doesn't just reveal; it transforms. That is why Scripture urges us to confess our sin and sometimes to lovingly speak truth to someone we care about.

"But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus, his Son, purifies us from all sin." (1 John 1:7)
There is no transformation without truth, and no truth without the light shining on it. The deepest experiences of God's love often come the moment our worst is exposed — and we discover His grace is still greater.

3. Walk with wisdom

"Be very careful, then, how you live — not as unwise but as wise, making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil... Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to debauchery. Instead, be filled with the Spirit." (Ephesians 5:15-18)

Knowledge is knowing facts; wisdom is applying them well in real situations. Because we live in spiritual enemy territory, we cannot stroll through life as if there is no battle. Paul's warning is pointed: don't be under the influence of alcohol — or anything else that dulls your judgment. The truth is, everyone is under the influence of something: media, culture, substances, the wrong voices. The question is simply, what is influencing you?

The alternative is to be continually filled with the Holy Spirit. You received the Spirit the moment you trusted Christ, but Paul urges an ongoing filling. How? Paul points to worship and gratitude: "always giving thanks to God the Father for everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ" (Ephesians 5:20). It is like stirring creamer into coffee — the moment you believe, you are filled, but fixing your heart daily on who Jesus is and what He has done stirs it through until you are truly changed.

A takeaway to carry into your week

If someone investigated your life this week, would there be enough evidence to prove you follow Jesus? The moon shines not with its own power but by reflecting the sun. In the same way, we stand out in a dark world only as we are filled with Christ's love and Spirit. So ask yourself honestly: What part of my life still needs to come into the light? Whatever it is, bring it to Him today — He sees you with eyes of love.
